questions.question: What did the people of her generation call Doña Gracia?
questions.explanation: A synagogue she established in Izmir was called simply "La Señora," without mentioning her name: evidence of her authority.

questions.question: True or false: Doña Gracia was born in Lisbon to a family of Anusim.
questions.explanation: Her parents were baptized by force in 1497, with all the Jews of Portugal, and kept the commandments in secret.

questions.question: True or false: Only when she reached bat mitzvah age did Doña Gracia learn that she was Jewish.
questions.explanation: The revelation shaped her world, and she devoted her life and her fortune to the rescue of her people.

questions.question: Whom did Doña Gracia marry in 1528?
options: Francisco Mendes, Tzemach Benveniste, head of an international trading house
questions.explanation: The trading house dealt in silver and spices, and especially in black pepper. The marriage was held in a secret Jewish ceremony and a public Christian ceremony.

questions.question: Which city granted her refuge in 1549, and there she returned openly to Judaism?
questions.explanation: Duke Ercole II recognized her inheritance rights, and she began to use the family name "Nasi."

questions.question: What was the "Ferrara Bible" (1553), which she supported?
options: A vocalized Hebrew edition for yeshivot
A Kabbalistic commentary on the Torah
A Latin translation for the Church
A translation of the Bible into Judeo-Spanish, for Anusim who did not know Hebrew
questions.explanation: The translation adhered to the structure of the Hebrew sentence and avoided Christian interpretations. It was officially dedicated to her.

questions.question: To which port was Jewish trade diverted in the Ancona boycott?
questions.explanation: The boycott came after Pope Paul IV burned at the stake Anusim who had returned to Judaism in Ancona, in 1556.

questions.question: Which of the great sages of Constantinople supported the boycott and ruled that the community may compel compliance with it?
questions.explanation: He saw her leadership as a legitimate political arm of the Jewish people in a time of crisis.

questions.question: True or false: The Maharashdam of Salonica supported the Ancona boycott wholeheartedly.
questions.explanation: He opposed the boycott, and feared for the fate of the Jewish communities in the Papal States.

questions.question: What did the opponents of the boycott fear?
options: That the Sultan would forbid trade with Europe
That the boycott would enrich Doña Gracia
That the Pope would take revenge on the communities in his state
That the Anusim would return to Christianity
questions.explanation: They also argued that merchants should not be forced to endanger their livelihood in the name of abstract solidarity.

questions.question: True or false: The Ancona boycott succeeded, and the Anusim who remained in the city were saved.
questions.explanation: Without halakhic consensus and with the opposition of merchants, among them merchants of Bursa, the boycott failed.

questions.question: True or false: Doña Gracia and Don Joseph Nasi first sought to lease Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: When the authorities refused, they leased Tiberias and its surroundings from Sultan Suleiman.

questions.question: Which industry did Doña Gracia plan in Tiberias so that its residents could make a living without donations?
options: A fishing port on the Kinneret
A silk industry, by planting mulberry trees
questions.explanation: The plan also included rebuilding the walls, houses for immigrants and a palace for Doña Gracia herself.

questions.question: What did Doña Gracia do for the bones of her husband, Francisco Mendes?
options: She obtained permission to transfer them for burial on the Mount of Olives
questions.explanation: The sages of the Land of Israel saw in this halakhic and familial self-sacrifice.

questions.question: In which city did Doña Gracia die?
questions.explanation: Her death prevented her from going up to Tiberias, as she had planned.

questions.question: True or false: After Doña Gracia's death the Tiberias enterprise continued and grew stronger.
questions.explanation: Without her dominant leadership the settlement enterprise faded.

questions.question: What was distinctive about the translation of the word "almah" (Isaiah 7:14) in the Jewish Ferrara Bible?
options: It was omitted from the translation
It remained "Alma" or was translated "young woman," and not "virgin" as in the Christian version
It was translated "virgin" as in the Church version
questions.explanation: So it emerged from the examination of 49 copies by Stanley Rypins: the printers prevented foreign theological distortion.

questions.question: What was the fate of Abraham Usque's printing house after it printed a lament for the martyrs of Ancona?
options: It moved to Constantinople under the Sultan's patronage
It received a prize from the Duke of Ferrara
Bishop Ghislieri ordered the book burned, and the printing house was closed
questions.explanation: The lament appeared in "Shiltei ha-Giborim" (Shields of the Heroes) by Rabbi Jacob of Fano. Ghislieri later became Pope Pius V.

questions.question: According to the research, why was her work downplayed after her death?
options: Fear that her figure would become an uncontrolled messianic focal point
Because she failed in the Ancona boycott
Because she was one of the Anusim
questions.explanation: The 16th century knew many false messiahs. Only at the end of the 20th century did her study and commemoration begin in Israel.

questions.question: What did Sultan Suleiman demand of the Pope, under her influence?
options: To open the ghetto of Rome
To release the prisoners who enjoyed Ottoman protection
To abolish the Inquisition in Portugal
questions.explanation: At the same time she sent Rabbi Yehuda Faraj to enlist the support of the rabbis for the boycott.
